decision-tradeoffs.title: Stay or move
decision-tradeoffs.intro: Weigh what each path could give and take.

career-manager-view.title: How might my manager see me?
career-manager-view.summary: Explore how work habits may signal trust, readiness, or concern.
career-manager-view.focus: How might my manager see me?

career-workplace-image.title: How might coworkers see me?
career-workplace-image.summary: Separate collaborative strengths from traits others may misread.

career-visible-contribution.title: Is my contribution visible?
career-visible-contribution.summary: Separate actual contribution from what the organization can readily see.
career-visible-contribution.focus:
Is my contribution visible?
First answer symbolically whether the contribution is being noticed, then why it is received that way. Do not claim a verified workplace evaluation or substitute a list of strengths.

career-manager-expectations.title: What might my manager expect?
career-manager-expectations.summary: Separate stated responsibilities from expectations I may be assuming.

career-stay-or-prepare.title: Should I stay or get ready to move?
career-stay-or-prepare.summary: Compare what is worth trying here with the effort of moving.
career-stay-or-prepare.focus: Should I stay or get ready to move?

career-opportunity-cost.title: What would I give up for this opportunity?
career-opportunity-cost.summary: Read the cost of taking this opportunity.
career-opportunity-cost.focus: What would I give up for this opportunity?

career-interview-strengths.title: Which strengths should I show in an interview?
career-interview-strengths.summary: Choose role-relevant evidence instead of listing every strength.
career-interview-strengths.focus: Which strengths should I show in an interview?

career-application-direction.title: Does my application direction fit me?
career-application-direction.summary: Read how this direction fits the way you work.
career-application-direction.focus:
Does my application direction fit me?
Read the symbolic fit or friction and why without inventing job conditions. Do not replace the judgment with general conditions for an ideal fit.

career-underused-strength.title: Which strength am I overlooking?
career-underused-strength.summary: Find where a familiar skill already helps your work.

career-growth-experience.title: What experience do I need next?
career-growth-experience.summary: Find the next experience that builds on what you do well.
career-growth-experience.focus: What experience do I need next?

career-role-fit.title: Does my current role fit my strengths?
career-role-fit.summary: Compare strengths I use well with what the role demands.
career-role-fit.focus:
Does my current role fit my strengths?
Read the symbolic fit or friction between strengths and role without inventing actual role terms. Do not substitute ideal-work conditions or automatic logging/experiments for the answer.

career-collaboration-role.title: What role do I repeat when teamwork gets hard?
career-collaboration-role.summary: Look past who is right to the roles and assumptions that repeat.
career-collaboration-role.focus: What role do I repeat when teamwork gets hard?

career-sustainable-boundary.title: Which work limit should I set first?
career-sustainable-boundary.summary: Find one lasting limit for time, responsibility, or communication.
career-sustainable-boundary.focus: Which work limit should I set first?

career-manager-mismatch.title: Why do my manager and I keep misaligning?
career-manager-mismatch.summary: Look for repeated differences in standards, reporting, and pace.
career-manager-mismatch.focus: Why do my manager and I keep misaligning?
